PlayStation says it "stepped away from the project" earlier this year, for undisclosed reasons. Read more
item.description:
It looks like Hideo Kojima has made some big changes behind-the-scenes with his upcoming "action espionage" title, Physint. The game, which was announced as a PlayStation exclusive in 2024, is now in the hands of Asha Sharma's Xbox, where Kojima will reportedly be a primary focus of her new vision for the platform. PlayStation says it "stepped away from the project" earlier this year, for undisclosed reasons.
"After careful consideration, we have made the difficult decision to step away from collaborating with Kojima Productions on Physint," says a post from PlayStation. "We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima's vision for the game. Our relationship remains strong after three decades of industry-leading, genre-defining creative cooperation, and we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future."
"Creators have choices about where and how they bring their ideas to life", says Asha Sharma in a post on the Xbox Wire. We’re honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on Physint. His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox."
It was only last summer that Hideo Kojima stated he was working on Physint all by himself, so a move like this suggests the game has at least entered another stage of production. Earlier this year, Kojima noted that Kojima confirmed that casting, scans, and performance capture sessions would kick off in 'late 2026'. We know from a report last year that the game was already casting actors, and had talent such as Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe attached.
https://www.youtube.com/embed/D8uF8VQVT7I
"As confirmed earlier through our official channels, in mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the Physint project," says Kojima in a tweet. "Physint is an important project both to me personally and to Kojima Productions. Determined to keep the project alive, we have spent the last three months searching tirelessly for a new partner. In the course of seeking advice and pursuing negotiations with people across many fields, we found in Xbox a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future, and we have decided to team up with them once again. Please rest assured that development of Physint, our genre-defining action-espionage title, is ongoing and will continue moving forward."
Kojima has previously made a big deal about the connection the game has to Columbia Pictures - notably, a division of Sony Interactive Entertainment sister company Sony Pictures. A shot of the studio, with a massive label for Physint emblazoned across its exterior walls - made up a large portion of the game's reveal. Will this collaboration be put in jeopardy now, or will Kojima Productions move the cinematic and camera-work to somewhere Microsoft-owned?
Perhaps Kojima's move to Xbox shouldn't come as a surprise: back in July 2026, we learned Kojima's other experimental in development game, OD, was reportedly safe from Microsoft cuts despite plenty of other studios and games facing the axe as part of Xbox's controversial 'reset' initiative. Maybe Xbox was more willing to invest in the game than Sony, a company which is also reassessing its video game investments as profit margins start to stagnate. Herman Hulst, CEO of Sony Interactive Entertainment, has previously backed Kojima's "next stage tactical espionage action game" publically, so whatever has soured between the two here is certainly noteworthy.
During Kojima Productions 10th anniversary livestream, the infamous creator noted that Physint is "just the start", a vague statement that could potentially hint at Kojima seeing franchise potential in the series - something that Xbox is interested in, no doubt, as some of its legacy studios and brands suffer as a result of recent industry contractions.
In 2025, Kojima noted the game won't be out for another "five or six" years, so if this is something Xbox is banking on, we can almost certainly expect it to be a marquee game for the as-yet-unrevealed Xbox Project Helix. The title was initially conceived during a period of sickness and surgery for Kojima, when thoughts of his own mortality convinced him to 'change his priorities' and go back to the action-espionage genre that helped make his name. Will the pivot back to the genre - and a partnership with an outwardly shaky Microsoft - pay off? We'll have to wait and see.

item.title: This week's dual-pronged Nintendo Direct shows were stuffed with huge games. Kirby and the World Beyond! Metroid Ravenous! The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time! But the Japanese version of today's show quietly snuck in at least one game the rest of us didn't get: a sequel to Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii's 1983 adventure game. Read more
item.description:
This week's dual-pronged Nintendo Direct shows were stuffed with huge games. Kirby and the World Beyond! Metroid Ravenous! The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time! But the Japanese version of today's show quietly snuck in at least one game the rest of us didn't get: a sequel to Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii's 1983 adventure game.
The Portopia Serial Murder Case came out a whopping 43 years ago - first on your personal computers, then on the NES - and the murder mystery romp went on to become a pretty big hit for Enix (now Square Enix). Even Hideo Kojima once credited it as one of the reasons why he wanted to begin making games in the first place.
And in today's Nintendo Direct, we got a brand-new trailer for a sequel to The Portopia Serial Murder Case. The text-based detective work and witness interrogations from the original seem to be intact, alongside a new string of murders. Check it out below.
The Steam page also notes that Yuji Horii is supervising the project as an executive director, though there's sadly no sign of English-language support just yet. We should hear more as the game approaches its 2027 release window on Switch 2 and PC.
"Set in 1980s Kobe, players can enjoy a completely new detective experience - investigating alongside a new cast of characters to uncover the secrets hidden behind the original murders," the Steam description explains. "This title is a menu-driven, command-selection text adventure game. Players utilize a variety of commands to navigate the investigation. By gathering witness statements and physical evidence, you will gradually uncover the truth behind the serial murders."
Three years back, Square Enix tried to revive the original game with an "educational demonstration of Natural Language Processing (NLP), an AI technology." That pseudo-remake, pseudo-experiment didn't go down too well with players - Steam reviewers slapped it with a 'Very Negative' rating. Although, Square Enix doesn't seem to be involved in this upcoming sequel.

item.title: The five-year wait for Valheim 1.0 doesn't seem to have hurt the survival game behemoth's popularity all that much. After leaving early access, the crafty viking sim is enjoying a huge resurgence in Steam player numbers. Read more
item.description:
The five-year wait for Valheim 1.0 doesn't seem to have hurt the survival game behemoth's popularity all that much. After leaving early access, the crafty viking sim is enjoying a huge resurgence in Steam player numbers.
Valheim's early access tenure ended earlier today, and it seems like lots of people were waiting for exactly the right time to jump into (or jump back into) the viral hit's adorably polygonal world. At the time of writing, around 160,000 folks are simultaneously playing Valheim's Steam version - the game hasn't reached such a huge crowd since April 2021. (Thanks, SteamDB.)
Still, Valheim hasn't been able to capture lightning in a bottle twice. At least, not yet. The game peaked over five years ago when 502,387 people logged on at the same time, aided by memes that sailed across the web and a playerbase that wasn't totally pandemic-free yet.
Today's Steam stats may also be skewed by the fact that Iron Gate's breakout game is now available to play on PS5, Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S consoles. The Valheim crowd on Steam no longer represents the entire Valheim crowd, then. We'll see how high those numbers soar as the game heads into its first proper weekend of release.
The Valheim 1.0 update arguably matches the game's incredible launch stats, too. Iron Gate's new patch notes are almost 1,800 words long and include too much new newness for me to neatly summarise here. Long story short, if you've not touched the procgen afterlife in a while, Valheim 1.0 adds a new biome called Deep North, over 40 fresh weapons, lots of new bits and bobs and hammers to craft, a graphics setting to stretch draw distances, and much more.

item.title: Around 1,900 unionised workers at Blizzard Entertainment have voted to ratify their first contract with the World of Warcraft publisher after years of negotiations. The union contract means Blizzard now has to bargain with staff over the use of generative-AI in game development, and workers also have better protection against any potential layoffs. Read more
item.description:
Around 1,900 unionised workers at Blizzard Entertainment have voted to ratify their first contract with the World of Warcraft publisher after years of negotiations. The union contract means Blizzard now has to bargain with staff over the use of generative-AI in game development, and workers also have better protection against any potential layoffs.
The contract covers all union-represented staff across the World of Warcraft, Warcraft Rumble, Hearthstone, Overwatch and Diablo teams, as well as people from Blizzard's QA, Platform and Technology, and Story and Franchise Development units. Some rare good news in the gaming world!
The Communications Workers of America labor union called the new contract "historic" in a recent press release and explained that Blizzard is now required to "discuss, evaluate, and bargain over the usage of artificial intelligence in the workplace." In a first for the video game industry, the contract has also given staff "the right to be 'recalled' into open positions across any Blizzard bargaining unit for 14 months from the date of their layoff announcement." Union members secured an extra four weeks of severance as part of the negotiations, as well, in the event of any layoffs.
"This contract marks the beginning of a new era at Blizzard Entertainment, but it doesn't stop with us. I look forward to the day that everyone in the industry can enjoy the protections that this contract affords us, like increased severance and recall rights in the event of a layoff and the ability to grieve injustices in the workplace," Overwatch QA worker Simon Hedrick said. "I believe that the positive change we have won will ripple out and help make the games industry as a whole a better place for workers and players alike. This contract is the start of something greater, and I urge everyone to remember: when we fight together, we win together."
Unionisation efforts within Blizzard Entertainment started many years ago, and have only grown exponentially over time. This latest win comes just months after Xbox cut 1,600 jobs across its subsidiaries, with 1,600 more to come, though the folks at Blizzard were seemingly unaffected this time around.
In a statement provided to Kotaku, Blizzard president Johanna Faries said the new agreement "marks a significant milestone and reflects our shared commitment to continuing to work together in support of our teams and our players."
Good timing, too - BlizzCon 2026 takes place this weekend and is sure to include looks at the future of several Blizzard games. Something funny's happening with the Starcraft website, which is probably a sign of things to come.

item.title: Sounds the alarms! A reveal trailer for a brand-new Kirby game has been revealed in today's Nintendo Direct. Called Kirby and the World Beyond, the game is headed to the Nintendo Switch 2 in Spring, 2027. Read more
item.description:
Sounds the alarms! A reveal trailer for a brand-new Kirby game has been revealed in today's Nintendo Direct. Called Kirby and the World Beyond, the game is headed to the Nintendo Switch 2 in Spring, 2027.
The game has a very vibrant, colourful aesthetic as is the norm with the Kirby series. Kirby is seen running through luscious green pastures, leaping across logs and other rushing across bridges. You can suck up enemies, of course, providing Kirby new abilities that come in handy during combat and open world traversal. Check out the trailer below.
Kirby's Sword Copy ability also be seen - a long-running with Kirby charging around with the Master Sword and using it to quickly ascend vertically. King Dedede is also present as a boss, who Kirby knocks through a Truman Show-style wall in the horizon. How mysterious!
On the topic of Zelda, that Link power up receives a massive power up in the second half of the trailer. In what appears to be a Tears of the Kingdom-specific modifier, Kirby can use his buffed-up Master Sword-looking upgrade to chop down trees and open up new pathways. Kirby also used it to break out into a very Hyrule-looking environment beyond the bounds of the vivid world they know. What is waiting for Kirby out there remains to be seen - the next world over does look very, very Zelda-inspired from here, though.
The game looks interesting! Who doesn't love a Kirby game, especially one that looks to have a lot of love (and resources) invested into it. The ties to Zelda seem like an interesting quirk - it feels as though some of the most interesting parts of the game may still be hidden.
Kirby and the World Beyond comes to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027, and will be just one part of a celebration Nintendo is planning for the lil' pink mascot's 35th anniversary.

item.title: Cast your mind back to December 2024, and you might remember a fun little tease for Overcooked studio Ghost Town Games' intriguing - and adorably spooky - co-op adventure Stage Fright. Closing in on two years later, the studio is back with some first proper gameplay ahead of its arrival next year. Read more
item.description:
Cast your mind back to December 2024, and you might remember a fun little tease for Overcooked studio Ghost Town Games' intriguing - and adorably spooky - co-op adventure Stage Fright. Closing in on two years later, the studio is back with some first proper gameplay ahead of its arrival next year.
Stage Fright, which has been in development for around five years now, follows its protagonists Drew, Blake and Charlie as they embark on a quest to solve an ancient mystery. And that's pretty much all of the set-up we're getting for now! What we do know, though, is that Ghost Town Games' spooky two-player action draws a touch of inspiration from Luigi's Mansion, as well as coming-of-age adventures like The Goonies and Stranger Things.
As for what that means more specifically, Stage Fright has been designed from the ground-up with communication-driven co-operation in mind. It's playable online or side-by-side in couch co-op, and sees players working together to overcome escape room-style conundrums and slightly more chaotic moments. It's also designed to be as approachable as possible, with Ghost Town Games explaining, "The challenge is in the mind, not the finger-tips!".
"When we set about thinking about our next game," it writes in its introduction to Stage Fright's latest look, "we wanted to continue our nostalgic love affair with Saturday nights in and fan the flame for an under-served couch co-op community. We also wanted to protect the one-button accessibility of Overcooked and resist the temptation to introduce dexterity at the expense of inclusivity. But we also wanted to take those Overcooked players out of the confines of the kitchen and off an adventure into a larger, more involving saga.
"In contrast to the fraught urgency of time-based levels, in Stage Fright, players can immerse themselves in a long-form mystery which requires them to work together to solve escape-room like puzzles, tackle strange and perplexing obstacles together and combine their mental agility to figure out what has happened in this strange town filled with odd characters."
And if you're wondering how three protagonists work with two players, the idea is you can switch between different pairs as you go, with Stage Fright's story unfolding from two perspectives - and judging by its new gameplay trailer, it's shaping up to be a bit of a spooky delight.
Ghost Town Games isn't talking platforms yet beyond Switch 1, Switch 2, and Steam, but Stage Fright - which is being published by No Man's Sky studio Hello Games - is set to arrive in "spring" next year.

item.title: During today's Nintendo Direct, the publisher and platform holder announced the next 2D Metroid game, called Metroid Ravenous. Read more
item.description:
During today's Nintendo Direct, the publisher and platform holder announced the next 2D Metroid game, called Metroid Ravenous.
The amazingly-titled game's first trailer showed us Samus being attacked by strange a variety of enemies that take her energy, as she seems to show a darker side of herself. "It's eat or be eaten," she says to an enemy at the end, with a concerning glint in her eye. It seems like a sequel to Mercury Steam's excellent Metroid Dread.
It’s eat…or be eaten. #MetroidRavenous. 28/01/2027. Only on #NintendoSwitch2. pic.twitter.com/b7f9fQWRmo
The game launches 28th January, 2027, and will come with a special edition two new amiibo figures. This isn't the first time we've heard about the game; it was initially leaked in a ratings board listing in Brazil.
Martin Robinson gave the previous game, Metroid Dread, a 5/5, calling the 2D title "A stylish, visually sumptuous return for 2D Metroid, and an adventure that proudly sits alongside the series' best". Ravenous looks set to continue where Dread left off, so here's hoping Mercury Steam and Nintendo can keep that level of quality alive.
It's also worth noting that the critically-acclaimed Nintendo Switch adventure seems to be the series' best-selling game: Metroid Dread shifted 2.9m copies worldwide in its first six months on sale, out-pacing the previous best-seller Metroid Prime. With that in mind, we can infer that both developer and publisher has had time (and money!) to cook with this title.

item.title: A new horror game from Bloober Team, best known for the Silent Hill 2 Remake and Cronos: The New Dawn, has been revealed at the Nintendo Direct. It's called Onyx: The Dark Grip, and it's coming next year. Read more
item.description:
A new horror game from Bloober Team, best known for the Silent Hill 2 Remake and Cronos: The New Dawn, has been revealed at the Nintendo Direct. It's called Onyx: The Dark Grip, and it's coming next year.
While a specific release window within 2027 has not yet been established, the game's reveal trailer does offer a peek at some interesting quirks. For one, the game features touchscreen and tilt mechanics that requires the game to be played in handheld mode, making this a scare you can take on the go.
Otherwise, the game places you in control of Holden, a man stuck in a town shrouded by fog after being "beckoned by a voice". While there, he'll have to uncover what's going on in this spooky locale, by either exploring sketchy looking places or reading the minds of other people he meets on his journey.
Bloober Team had announced they were working on a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, and this reveal shows the studio's delving back into its smaller-scope development roots. In recent years, Bloober Team has had its hands full with larger scale games which have all been received rather well. The Silent Hill 2 Remake was of course a big hit, and Cronos seems to have gone down well too. Here's hoping Onyx shares a similar fate.

item.title: Monster Hunter Wilds is coming to the Nintendo Switch 2, it has just been revealed during the Nintendo Direct. Read more
item.description:
Monster Hunter Wilds is coming to the Nintendo Switch 2, it has just been revealed during the Nintendo Direct.
The game, with all its free DLC updates (including new monsters), will be included in this console port. Nintendo fans will be able to pick it up starting the 5th December.
This version of the game is also coming with local co-op support, much like the older games in the series did, so you can venture out to your friends' house in real life and get a hunting party going.
In addition, the Nintendo Direct trailer reminded viewers that Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascension is on the way. This, the first major expansion to Wilds, is bringing a new hunting region, new story quests, and of course new monsters.
If you've never played Monster Hunter Wilds, Eurogamer's review from last year found it was "The most exhilarating and refined Monster Hunter yet". Since then, the game has only received more updates and improvements, so this Switch 2 might be a good chance to hop in.

item.title: Meccha Chameleon, the indie hide-and-seek game that launched on Steam a couple of months ago, is already one of the year's biggest hits, taking the PC market by storm. Now, as revealed in today's Nintendo Direct, the indie smash hit is coming to Nintnedo Switch 2 - and it arrives today. Read more
item.description:
Meccha Chameleon, the indie hide-and-seek game that launched on Steam a couple of months ago, is already one of the year's biggest hits, taking the PC market by storm. Now, as revealed in today's Nintendo Direct, the indie smash hit is coming to Nintnedo Switch 2 - and it arrives today.
Hopefully on the Switch 2 version, we aren't going to see any of those user-made maps that were found to contain malware. The issue was resolved fairly quickly, but marred what has otherwise been a fairly positive run for the unlikely viral hit.
Meccha Chameleon topped a staggering 15 million sales in less than a month, and I imagine coming to Nintendo Switch is just going to keep the game's remarkable momentum going. Meccha Chameleon is the latest in a string of delightful social co-op games, following in the footsteps of the likes of REPO, Lethal Company, and Among Us. Like those games before it, Meccha Chameleon is being sold for a relatively low price compared to many of the triple-A offerings. It's currently available for £5.29 on Steam - but I will let you know how much it'll cost on Nintendo Switch 2. I doubt it will be lots more.
Meccha Chameleon's simple hook has made it a hit with streamers and fans of social co-op games. The game plays as an elaborate prop hunt where players paint themselves to blend into the environment. Rather than simply hiding among the clutter, the ability to paint your character introduces an element of creativity that's part of what made it so popular.

item.description:
We should stop meeting like this! Yes, for the second time in two days, our fates have become intertwined thanks to the matchmaking of Nintendo. Following yesterday's 40th anniversary Legend of Zelda showcase, we got to do the announcement livestream thing all over again - and this time for a proper Nintendo Direct, which managed to squeeze an enormous amount of stuff into its 45-minutes focused on games arriving this "winter".
So what did it bring? Well, arguably the biggest news is there's a brand-new 2.5D Metroid on the way, and it's coming early next year. But Kirby fans also have something to look forward to as the pink puffball takes his turn at going open-world in Kirby and the World Beyond. Elswhere, we got word of a free Mario Kart World update bringing retro tracks to multiplayer, a free multiplayer update for Star Fox, as well as a long-awaited release for Professor Layton and The New World of Steam. Perhaps surprisingly though, we didn't get the long-awaited release date for FromSoftware's The Duskbloods despite its recent, and extremely promising, network test.
Returning to the stuff we actually got though, you'll find everything announced in September's Nintendo Direct below.
Monster Hunter Wilds was good, PC performance issues and a few other niggles aside. And we now know it's coming to Switch 2 on 4th December. Furthermore, its upcoming Ascendance expansion is on the way too and launching next year.
Wondering when the Final Fantasy remake series is concluding on Switch 2? Well wonder no more: Nintendo has confirmed Revelation, the third part of the saga, hits its console on 8th April next year. Additionally, should you need a Final Fantasy fix sooner, Crisis Core Final Fantasy 7 Reunion is coming to Switch 2 later today.
Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity - the second entry in Koei Tecmo's Zelda-themed hack-and-slash spin-off series - is making its way to Switch 2 in the form of a Definitive Edition. It's promising the likes of 60fps support, more enemies on screen, plus all the content from Age of Calamity's expansion pass. And there's also a tougher Calamity mode. It's launching 25th February next year, and there's a digital discount for owners of the Switch 1 version.
If you enjoyed the multiplayer parts of Switch 2's recent Star Fox 64 remake, there's some good news. It's about to get four-player split-screen support (which also means four players can join a team on one console and play online battles together) and new multiplayer stages, themed around Katina, Sector X, and Venom. The free update arrives on 30th September this year.
Meccha Chameleon has been a smash hit, and Switch 2 owners will soon have the opportunity to try their hand at its silly team-based hide-and-seek action. It launches on Switch 2 today!
After taking us deep beneath the waves, Pokémon Pokopia's expansion is, next, going a little bit simpler but a lot more fashionable, with a selection of Pokémon-themed accessories. We already knew this was the case for part two of three, but Nintendo has now given us a peek at what's to come, showing everything from ribbons to bowties. Plus, there'll be a couple more Pokémon joining in the fun when Part 2 launches "late 2026".
CD Projekt's spruced up version of The Witcher 3 - which includes both previous expansions - is coming to Switch 2 on 29th September. New stuff includes "enhanced visuals and gameplay", alongside support for mouse and motion controls, gyro aiming and touchscreen. Additionally, the game's brand-new expansion, Songs of the Past, launches next year. Woo!
Warhorse Studios' 2025 action-RPG sequel Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is heading to Switch 2 in a new Royal Edition form. It bundles together the base game and all previous DLC - adding the likes of new stories and outfits - and it arrives sometime in 2027.
Not much to report on this one. Switch 2's new Fire Emblem instalment, Fortune's Weave, quickly popped in to remind everyone it's launching 17th September. Thanks!
Amazingly, it's been three years since developer Level-5 announced it would be revisiting one of its most beloved series in Professor Layton and the New World of Steam. At the time, it was due to launch for Switch, but in the years since, it's also been confirmed to arrive on Switch 2 (as well as PS5 and PC). I've been excited to return to the world of Luke and Layton ever since that initial reveal, so I'm delighted to learn it's finally almost upon us, with a release date now set for 10th December this year.
Exactly that: Level-5 followed up its Professor Layton announcement with word that Yo-Kai Watch 2: Haunted Domain is in development for Switch 2. Did it have anything else to add? Only this: "It'll take a while meowre!"
If you were wondering why Pikmin 4 got a free update for Switch 1 last year that didn't include any notable upgrades for Switch 2, here's your answer: Nintendo's just announced its flogging the game again as a new Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition. Among other things, it adds the ability to give voice commands to Oatchi using the console's built-in mic and you can praise him too. There's also a new Dandori Academy mode challenging you to secure treasure as quickly as possible. The idea is you'll need to practice ahead of a proper "exam" scheduled for Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, and you only get one attempt. It's coming 12th November, and owners of the Switch 1 version can purchase a digital upgrade.
Bloober Team, the studio behind the likes of Layers of Fear and the Silent Hill 2 remake, is bringing a new handheld-focused horror game to Switch 2. Onyx: The Dark Grip sees its protagonist, Holden, visiting a fog-shrouded town "steeped in mystery", and players can interact with his adventure using the touchscreen to do things like unlock doors and read minds. The trouble is, Holden perceives your actions as those of a supernatural entity, and you'll need to avoid sending him over the edge as you play. It's out next year.
Overcooked studio Ghost Town Games announced its new co-op adventure Stage Fright a while back, and we've now had our first proper look at gameplay courtesy of Nintendo's latest Direct. There's no release date for it yet, but it's coming to Switch 1, Switch 2, and PC.
Ever wanted to be a merperson? Then your wish, with a wave of the Disney wand, is about to come true. Disney Dreamlight Valley is heading under the waves for its next expansion, the Keepsake Sea, which is launching this November.
It wouldn't be a Nintendo Direct without more amiibo to fill your dwindling shelfspace. And this latest showcase confirmed two new Kirby Air Riders figures - Sword Kirby & Dragoon, plus Noir Dedede & Hyra - are launching 12th November, completing the Air Riders amiibo line-up. Additionally, another in-game event, with related rewards, is on the way to the game, with more news due at a later date.
There are two things you need to know about developer The Game Bakers' survival-adjacent climbing game Cairn: it's blimmin' excellent, and also blimmin' hard. It turns out I probably wouldn't last an afternoon on the mysterious Mount Kami, but at least Cairn's protagonist Aava has a much firmer grip on things. That's a climbing joke, by the way. And now the point of all this: Cairn is coming to Switch 2 early next year, but you don't need me to tell you how good it is. Because a demo is releasing on the eShop today.
Capcom's acclaimed remakes of Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 3, and Resident Evil 4 are all making their way to Switch 2, with all their DLC included. They'll be available digitally initially, launching for eShop on 16th October, but physical editions release on 29th January next year.
Lara Croft's very first adventure is getting the remake treatment for a second time in its three-decade history, courtesy of developers Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog. And a Switch 2 release has now been confirmed. It's called Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, and while some of the choices being made for this reimagining aren't especially encouraging, we'll know how it's all come together when it releases on 12th February next year.
It's got sports, it's on Switch 2, and it's still releasing on 22nd October. That's all!
Goodness! I certainly wasn't expecting to see Samus back so soon, but the bounty hunter is making a return in Metroid Ravenous, which looks to follow the same 2.5D stylings as 2021's excellent Metroid Dread. It's coming to Switch 2 on 28th January next year, alongside a special edition and an amiibo.
Mario Kart World features a number of classic courses sneakily tucked around its expansive map, and these'll soon be playable in VS race mode, courtesy of a free new update. Expect to be careening around the likes of Choco Island 1, Vanilla Lake 1, Ghost Valley 1, and seven more - complete with working question mark panels - when the update arrives today. And that's not quite everything: two new routes - Turnip Rally and Propeller Rally - join Knockout World Tour.
Mega Man: Dual Override is coming to Switch 1&2 in spring next year, and to mark the occasion, we got a quick bit of new gameplay showcasing returning ally Proto Man who's joining the adventure in playable form. New amiibo of the pair launch alongside the game.
As is Nintendo Direct tradition, things started to get a bit chaotic once we hit the 'montage' section. Which, I regret to admit, is the point my speedtyping prowess utterly failed me. We also got a few other bits around the montage I couldn't quite keep up with, so to keep things simple, here's everything tucked into the montage - and around the montage - complete with links to each trailer where applicable, and their respective release dates. Enjoy!
There are good time ahead for fans of the Persona series on Switch 2. Not only is Persona 4's highly anticipated remake, Persona 4 Revival, coming to the console on 20th May next year, Nintendo has confirmed Persona 6 is also on the way.
Well, the bad news is we didn't get a release date for The Duskbloods, but the good news is Nintendo's buoyant pink puffball is back to upside-down those frowns. Kirby is making his return in a brand-new 3D adventure, Kirby and the World Beyond, that's coming to Switch 2 in spring 2027. There's not much more to say about this one just yet, other than that it'll apparently let players "freely explore" while using Kirby's powers. But its arrival coincides with the series' 35th anniversary, so expect more details on that soon.

item.description:
Opinion seems to be favourable about Witcher-like dark fantasy role-playing game The Blood of Dawnwalker - barring a few technical problems, that is. Quibbles with performance issues, controller issues, and bugs (and perhaps the lack of a New Game+ mode) are holding the game back. To this end, developer Rebel Wolves has whisked out a quick hotfix, addressing some of the issues at hand.
Rebel Wolves has also been spotted advertising for a lead writer (via Resetera) to help create a Blood of Dawnwalker sequel, which is something the studio talked openly about wanting to make even before the game was released. Indeed, I spoke to game director and studio co-founder Konrad Tomaszkiewicz about exactly this - about the studio's plan to follow vampire hero Coen through historical eras in new adventures, and about our ability as players to carry our saved games over.
The hotfix (1.04), which is rolling out now on all platforms - PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X - addresses stability issues, quest-blocking issues, game-saving issues, and specific Steam controller issues.
The controller fix relates to a drop in frame-rate when plugging a controller in, using what the hotfix notes called "outdated GameInput software", which is I believe the software Windows uses to recognise devices like controllers being plugged in. Rebel Wolves also made more adjustments to controller dead zones to avoid issues when sprinting - an issue I've seen players mention a lot.
These changes follow a hotfix from the weekend which added formal DualSense controller support on Steam and GOG. I don't know if this has fixed the issue with dialogue choice and inventory navigation jumping around when using a controller, which is very annoying.
The stability fixes, meanwhile, are simply listed as "multiple improvements to the game's stability". There's no sign yet of uncapped frame-rates in cutscenes that people are asking for, nor performance optimisation across a range of resolutions and graphics cards. An earlier hotfix did attempt to address Borderless and Windowed game performance, though.
Notably, Rebel Wolves has pledged to keep improving the game until the work is done. "We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy The Blood of Dawnwalker more comfortably. Thank you for your support and patience," the studio wrote in the 1.02 hotfix Steam post.
The Blood of Dawnwalker was released last week, and in my Eurogamer review, I was enthusiastic about it. "CD Projekt Red alumni create a familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful," I wrote. The game has already passed 1m sales, experiencing a strong overlap, perhaps unsurprisingly, with a Witcher 3 audience. How much higher can the sales go, I wonder?

Which mean, among other things, alliances, orbital bases, the ability to purchase and live in your own space station, and you can finally fly to the sun. Read more
item.description:
After much teasing and speculation, No Man's Sky's 10th anniversary Cosmos update is here and, yup, it's a big 'un, bringing a "complete overhaul of space". Which mean, among other things, alliances, orbital bases, the ability to purchase and live in your own space station, and you can finally fly to the sun.
"No Man's Sky is often referred to as 'a Space Game'," explains Hello Games in its Cosmos unveiling. "It's a huge part of our game, but we've never really updated space since release. In most sci-fi games, space is just an empty void. With Cosmos we wondered - can we make space feel truly alive? And could we make space feel more like home? What if you could own a space station? If you could build star bases, and create alliances with other players."
And that's what today's update brings. As far as space station ownership goes, once you've purchased one in your solar system of choice, you can decorate it inside and out then invite your friends to enjoy your creative whims.
Alternatively, you can now build free-floating modular bases anywhere in space, with Hello Games suggesting you might like to create your own starship truck stop, military outpost, or perhaps even an orbital restaurant at the end of - well you know how that goes.
Asteroid belts, meanwhile, have had a bit of a do-over, and can now consist of both rock and ice formations that provide intrepid space wanderers with valuable crystal resources. Some rare asteroids are even large enough to land on - which does, of course, mean they're also large enough to build on...
And scanning a new system on entry means you might find new points-of-interest among the stars. Space now contains its own outposts, for instance, where you can trade with alien lifeforms, buy maps, get information about the area, take on new missions, and more.
Additionally, you'll find space hulks that can be stripped and salvaged using the gravity gun. Any scrap you successfully secure can be thrown at your ship's newly introduced tractor beam, but some caution is required. Get too greedy, and you might cause the hulk to melt down and explode. Elsewhere, space now contains bio-wrecks, some of which have been overwhelmed by biological hazards that may need to be cleared out in order to reclaim. And finally, there's the system's sun, which - for the first time since launch - is apparently now reachable, although a "perilous journey" awaits those who try.
And tying all this together, as if there wasn't already enough to be getting on with, is a new alliance system. "As an alliance," explains Hello, "you can work together to build a networked empire of different stations and rise the new leaderboards to compete for the largest, richest, or most prominent alliance."
But we're still not quite done. In one final 10th anniversary flourish, today's release arrives alongside a new limited-time expedition. It's called - echoing No Man's Sky's long-standing mantra - 'Our Journey Continues', and seeing players working toward different milestones that each represents one of the exploratory space sim's 40 major updates since launch in 2016.
So there you go! No Man's Sky's Cosmos update launches today on all platforms (that's - brace yourself - PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 1&2, Mac, PSVR 1&2, PC VR and Game Pass), and full patch notes can be found on Hello Games' website. And if you're in the mood for a bit more celebratory reading, Eurogamer recently spoke to the No Man's Sky players building utopia at the end of the universe - and it's a fascinating story.

item.title: It's day-two of Nintendo's Direct September showcases, and today the focus is Switch games arriving this winter. Today's show begins at 3pm UK time and we'll be covering the big announcements here, live, as they happen. Read more
item.description:
It's day-two of Nintendo's Direct September showcases, and today the focus is Switch games arriving this winter. Today's show begins at 3pm UK time and we'll be covering the big announcements here, live, as they happen.
What do we expect? Nintendo showed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake yesterday in some detail, so I expect that means Zelda is cleared from the board. That does leave room for another major Nintendo franchise to take centre stage, like, perhaps, Mario. We haven't had a mainline 3D Mario game since Odyssey in 2017, nearly 10 years ago, so one is well overdue, though the Odyssey team was busy making Donkey Kong Bananza in the time since. With Nintendo specifying a "winter" focus for this showcase, however, a glimpse at a far-away Mario game might be wishful thinking.
What we can all-but guarantee, though, is a release date for FromSoftware's The Duskbloods, which we know is coming this year but not when. Would an October release date be too soon? Would it dare go close to GTA 6 in mid-November? It's a tricky time for a game.
There's also hope of Nintendo revealing a long-awaited Switch 2 version of Diablo 4 ahead of BlizzCon this weekend, and I'm sure we'll see some footage of Witcher 3 Remastered on Switch 2, after its Gamescom reveal last week.
We're almost certain to see more of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, too, which releases next week for Switch 2. Nintendo has already shown off plenty of footage from this game, but maybe we'll see even more either in the Direct, or in the Nintendo Treehouse that will last a whopping 110 minutes after the show is concluded.
But beyond that? I'm less sure. The "winter" period technically takes us to the end of February, so there's room for things we don't perhaps yet know about. Let's see.
Our live coverage of this event has finished.
And I am absolutely certainly NOT hoping for any news on a new F-zero game. You hear that Nintendo?! (crosses fingers that this new inverse psychology tactic will work out).
We're nearing the off. Shigeru Miyamoto has slipped his plushie Yoshi slippers on and picked up his Mario mushroom pipe (steady). What has Nintendo got in store?
Good shout! You certainly can hope.
Time is ticking, Here's a question for you: has it been a good year for Switch?
I wonder if The Duskbloods date really is the end of September. That would be wild. That's too close, surely?
We're getting close to the off here. Nintendo is really pushing Splatoon Raiders on the pre-show.
Donkey Kong Bananaza, the FFVII games, Splatoon Raiders, Culdcept Begins, Tiny Book Club - all crackers.
We are minutes, maybe seconds away from the show beginning now. What will we open with?
Monster Hunter Wilds on Switch 2 opens the show
The familiar Nintendo Director 3D shapes are forming into a logo. There was a PEGI 18 logo - exciting.
Monster Hunter Wilds opens the show. We've not seen this running on Switch 2 before. If this is Switch 2 footage, and why wouldn't it be, then it looks pretty good.
MH Wilds gets an early December release date and local play
The Switch 2 version includes local play, which is a winning addition. Never forget the effect Monster Hunter had on the PSP because of mulitplayer.
FF7 Reunion Crisis Core launches on Switch 2 today
Nintendo's Koizumi is here to lead us through the show. The first announcement: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation running on Switch 2. It's coming 8th April. That was announced last week. So we knew this.
The prequel to FF7 - Crisis Core - FF7 Reunion, launching on Switch 2 later today.
A Switch 2 version of Zelda Hyrule Warriors is coming, with better performance and a harder difficulty mode. 25th February edition for the Definitive Edition of Age of Calamity.
Meccha Chameleon is coming to Switch 2 today
Meccha Chameleon is coming to Switch! The Steam sensation of 2026 - a game about blending into your surroundings and hiding - is making its way to Nintendo's handheld.
Zipping into a Pokémon Pokopia update now. Very incidental season expansion pass updates here. There are accessories coming, then there's a new town later on.
Free Star Fox update brings four-player split-screen
A free update for Star Fox is coming 30th September. Battle Mode is expanding with four-player local split-screen play, either to fight against each other or team up as a four and go online.
Three new stages are also being added.
GameCube game Star Fox Adventures is also out today on Nintendo Classics.
The Witcher 3 on Switch 2 has unique Joy-Con controls, and Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 is coming
A Witcher 3 Remastered edition nod here. It looks pretty good running on Switch 2, and it apparently comes with gyroscopic aiming, Joy-Con 2 mouse controls and touch screen support. If you have the Switch version of The Witcher 3, you can upgrade for free.
Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 is also coming to Switch 2 in a Royal Edition that launches next year. It includes the base game, all premium story expansions, exclusive gear and a bonus questline. The gameplay footage looked a little choppy, though.
New Professor Layton coming in December
Professor Layton! There's a new game on the way with the biggest collection of puzzles yet, apparently.
Professor Layton and the New World of Steel coming 10th December.
Says a press release: "Layton and his trusted assistant Luke return in an all-new instalment of the puzzle-solving adventure series set at the dawn of the industrial age. After receiving a letter from Luke, the professor travels to Steam Bison, a rapidly developing American town plagued by mysterious incidents. Solve puzzles, uncover clues and follow the duo’s search for the truth when Professor Layton and the New World of Steam launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch on December 10th."
There's a new Yo-kai Watch in development
There's a new Yo-kai Watch in development. We saw a brief teaser for it. Yo-kai Watch 2: Haunted Domain it was called. No release date.
A press release said: "The latest entry in the Yo-kai Watch series evolves the adventures of Yo-kai Watch 2: Bony Spirits, Fleshy Souls and Psychic Specters with enhanced graphics and new content on Nintendo Switch 2. Join Nate as he befriends a wide variety of Yo-kai and embarks on the mysterious adventures that define the series. Along with new story content, players may even encounter some new Yo-kai. Additional details will be shared in the future."
Pikmin 4 Switch 2 edition launches in November
A Pikmin 4 update for Switch 2 now. There's new voice commands for your dog using the Switch 2's built-in microphone. And there's something called Dandori Academy, where you can test yourself in treasure hunts and stages with exams every Friday, Saturday and Sunday. There are 72 Dandori Academy stages planned for release over time.
The Switch 2 edition and the Dandori Academy launch 12th November.
Bloober's Switch 2-exclusive horror game revealed
Ooh ooh. A scary game. A manky apartment, an edgy voice over. A man looking in a mirror. I don't recognise this.
Onyx: The Dark Grip - this is Bloober's presumably Switch-exclusive horror. You can read minds in the game. It's a kind of side-scroller but also isometric at points. A more simplistic game, graphically speaking. Looks like it has interesting ideas.
Okay, it is exclusive to Switch 2. It's coming next year.
Says a press release: "Survive as a vessel and interfere as a god in this 2.5D supernatural horror game developed by Bloober Team exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2. Play as the mysterious Entity, guiding the actions of a lone traveller who arrives in a desolate ghost town. Manipulate the environment with your supernatural powers, solve puzzles, confront terrifying creatures and don’t let your puppet descend into the depths of madness. Blur the line between the game world and reality when Onyx: The Dark Grip launches for Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027."
Xenoblade Chronicles 3 Switch 2 edition arrives in December
A Switch 2 version of Xenoblade Chronicles 3 is coming with a new Heroes Vault mode, which looks a bit like a twin-stick shooter - that sort of presentation.
There's also a new hero coming to the game - Shimmer.
Overcooked team's new game Stage Fright looks good
Stage Fright now, from the Overcooked team. Matt has some information about this about to share in a moment. This looks pretty good. 2027 for this.
That is a good way of describing it!
Apparently the trailer said it's playable exclusively in handheld mode.
LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight swoops in. I'm still yet to play this - it looks great. It's got local co-op, and it includes the DLC released so far.
18th September, that's coming.
Ondeh! That's what it was called. This one whizzed by.
A press release describes Ondeh Ondeh Kaya's Tasty Tale as a rhythm-puzzle action adventure, made by the studio Metronomik in Kuala Lumpur. It's inspired by the vibrancy of Southeast Asia, apparently, and it's coming to PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X.
More amiibos are on their way. Don't ask me to describe them. Something to do with Kirby. Does anyone collect amiibo here?
Oh, it looks like Cairn is coming to Switch 2!
Climbing game Cairn is coming to Switch 2
We liked Cairn, and I hear a lot of good things about it. It launches "early 2027". And there's a demo being added to the eShop today.
The Resident Evil remakes are coming to Switch 2 in October
The Resident Evil Remakes are coming to Switch 2. That's Resident Evil 2 Deluxe Edition, Resident Evil 3, and Resident Evil 4 Gold Edition. Those fancy editions include more content than the base games did.
The digital editions of all three games launch 16th October, with physical editions scheduled for 29th January.
The Tomb Raider remake! That people seem a bit down on so far. It's coming to Switch 2. No sign of the RPG stuff here. 12th Feb for this.
Nintendo Switch Sports Resort now. I'm so up for this. You can chase dolphins in the ocean! Search for hibiscus flowers! I don't know what this means but it seems wholesome.
Wii Bowling still remains a fond memory of mine.
22nd October for Switch Sports Resort.
A new Metroid game announced for a January release
Moving on, we've got a lady's voice over saying she was attacked. We're in a futuristic desert fantasy world. Metroid?! Goodness, I didn't expect that.
A new Metroid Dread from MercurySteam? This looks a bit more colourful, maybe?
It looks breakneck in terms of spead, and the perspective seems to change often, from 2D to 3D to fighting game.
Metroid Ravenous. And it's out 28th January! MercurySteam is not confirmed as the developer yet, and hasn't said anything on its social media.
A Metroid amiibo collection will release at the same time, apparently, with Samus and Chozo statues. And a Samus (Metroid suit) amiibo will be exclusive to the special edition of the game.
Mario Kart World gets SNES tracks in a free update today
Well, that was a surprise banger from Nintendo!
A Mario Kart World free update now and it's bringing courses from the SNES Mario Kart game.
Says a press release: "Classic courses from Super Mario Kart have been hiding in plain sight across the continent of Mario Kart World, and now 10 of them can be played as standalone races in VS Race. Tear through Choco Island, Vanilla Lake, Ghost Valley and more, complete with ? Panels that grant items just like in the Super NES original. The update also adds two new Knockout Tour routes, Propeller Rally and Turnip Rally, plus a Spectator Mode when playing with friends online*3 or via LAN Play*4. The free update is available later today."
There's a new Mega-Man game called Dual Override. It looks... I'm not sure how it looks. A bit cheap? It's coming in spring 2027. Maybe I'm being harsh.
Octopath-like RPG Eternal Anima now. It looks exactly like you'd imagine: a turn-based RPG with micro people and dinky but lavish graphics. 4th march for that.
Danganronpa 2x2 is getting a wonderfully titled Slayhem mode. 14th Janaury, it's coming, on both Switch consoles.
The Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves is coming to Switch 2. 22nd October.
SNK is also bringing Metal Slug series to Switch 2. This looks fantastic. It's the Ultimate Collection and it's coming next year.
These announcements are whizzing past. Yu-Gi-Oh something or other now. It's got fully voiced dialogue, online multiplayer, and characters that say "sweet". Tag-Force GX. 16th February.
Romancing Saga 3 is coming 16th February 2027.
Stellar Blade is coming to Switch 2, and It Takes Two has been updated
007 First Light is coming this year (strange that it hasn't got a more firm date yet if that's the case). Far Cry 3 is coming spring 2027. Far Cry 3 Blood Dragon is also coming spring 2027. The Crew Motorfest 8th October.
House Flipper in October. Sonic Pico Park 12th November. Dragon Quest Monsters 3rd December and a demo available later today.
Hela coming 1st December. There are some games I have no idea about here.
Eriksholm! 3rd December. Stellar Blade Complete Edition 5th November.
It Takes Two 15th October. A press release says the Switch 2 version has a higher resolution, a better frame-rate, and cross-platform play. You can use GameShare on Switch as well. Existing owners of It Takes Two on Switch can upgrade to the Switch 2 version for free.
These announcements are racing past. Hell is Us, 8th October. Guardians of the Galaxy, 5th November.
Presona 4 Revival arrives a few months later on Switch 2, and Persona 6 is confirmed
And we pause to break to Atlus and what may be a Persona game.
Personal 4. The remake. This looks sharp and colourful. It's coming out notably later on Switch 2 - 20th May. It comes out 18th February on other platforms.
Persona 6! But it's just a logo.
Says a press release: "Persona 6 brings the series’ signature blend of daily life, social bonds and supernatural adventure to an all-new standalone story featuring a fresh cast of characters."
A new 3D open-world Kirby game closes the show
Is that just confirmation that Persona 6 is coming to Switch 2? I guess so.
ANd the last announcement is... A colourful green, cutesy world. Kirby? It is Kirby.
A 3D open-world Kirby puzzling game. Who needs Mario, hey?
Kirby and the World Beyond, this is called, and it looks very colourful and energetic. It's exclusive to Switch 2 and it's coming Spring 2027.
We can freely explore the world, apparently. Next year will mark the 35th anniversary of Kirby, apparently.
That is very good way of putting it.
Good point! That is bizarre. Unless... Don't say it. Unless it's going to slip to next year.
No release date for The Duskbloods, worryingly
The conspicuous absence from the showcase was, of course, the lack of a release date for FromSoftware's The Duskbloods. What does this mean? The worry is, of course, that we're potentially looking at a delay to 2027 for the game. Did the problems encountered during the recent network test worry From?
If you're just joining us, you can catch up with everything announced in the Nintendo Direct in a separate article, if you don't want to scroll back through this one. Up to you!
Thank you everyone for joining us again today. I've updated the feed with lots of videos and information from press releases.

item.title: Elden Ring is in the conversation again thanks to its Tarnished Edition release on Switch 2. To coincide with the launch of the long-awaited port, FromSoftware released a DLC pack for other platforms including the extras from this Switch 2 Tarnished Edition. Read more
item.description:
Elden Ring is in the conversation again thanks to its Tarnished Edition release on Switch 2. To coincide with the launch of the long-awaited port, FromSoftware released a DLC pack for other platforms including the extras from this Switch 2 Tarnished Edition.
Shortly after the DLC went live, however, players figured out a way to duplicate the items it contains, making it possible to give copies to players who don't own the add-on. In response, FromSoftware has deployed an emergency Elden Ring patch, the sole purpose of which is to plug that security hole.
Patch 1.17.1 arrived Tuesday, 8th September on all platforms. "This update fixes an issue in multiplayer where, under specific conditions, DLC-specific items could be obtained when not normally eligible. No additional content is included," the announcement post on X read.
The $5 / £4 Tarnished Pack includes two new starting classes - Idus Knight and Heavy Knight - as well as new armour sets and weapons. It also comes with new skins for your goaty horse mount Torrent.
The glitch worked by having a player who owned the DLC join the game of someone who didn't, then drop the items for the other person to pick up. This didn't remove them from the original player's inventory, hence it being a duplication exploit.
Though the patch fixed the issue, it did not prevent item trading altogether. Items - including DLC-exclusive weapons and armours - can still be traded between players, but doing so will now correctly remove it from the original player's inventory.
In Eurogamer's impressions of Elden Ring on Switch 2, Kelsey Raynor was impressed with how the developer managed to get it all working on Nintendo's console, even if the game's performance isn't flawless.

item.title: A massive information leak appears to have pushed full achievement lists for upcoming and unannounced PC games, including Persona 6 and Kingdom Hearts 4, onto the internet. Read more
item.description:
A massive information leak appears to have pushed full achievement lists for upcoming and unannounced PC games, including Persona 6 and Kingdom Hearts 4, onto the internet.
The lists were scraped and added to various websites, including SteamDB and achievement tracking website Exophase overnight. X3sphere, the owner of Exophase, told ResetEra they believed the leak was the result of a "possible screw up on Valve's end", after the Steam API seemingly gained access to achievement lists that should be private.
"I usually never see games without an actual name pop up with achievements," X3sphere continued, "yet over the past hour or so a bunch have (when there's an unknown name we just set it to the AppID)."
While the full scope of this apparent - and as yet unconfirmed - leak remains unclear, the number of games seemingly impacted or revealed is vast. It also means spoilers are rife. Reddit user KingdomHeartsII wrote up a list of the games that have been found so far, including more than a dozen that are yet to be announced at all.
It's worth noting that some of these achievement lists do include potential spoilers. So if, for example, you're a diehard Kingdom Hearts or Megaman fan, you probably shouldn't go and take a peek at the leaks if you want to go in without anything ruined ahead of time, just in case they are legitimate.

item.title: The Total War: Warhammer 40,000 team at Creative Assembly has an interesting challenge on its hands. How do you create a game that lives up to the series' reputation as a deep tactical adventure while building a strong enough on-ramp for those new to the Total War series and to Warhammer as a whole? item.description:
The Total War: Warhammer 40,000 team at Creative Assembly has an interesting challenge on its hands. How do you create a game that lives up to the series' reputation as a deep tactical adventure while building a strong enough on-ramp for those new to the Total War series and to Warhammer as a whole?
The answer, says Creative Assembly, is Total War: Warhammer 40,000 - what it's calling both the most complex and most accessible game it's ever made. How could both possibly be true? To find out, I spoke with Joy Dey, design lead on Total War: Warhammer 40,000's tutorial campaigns and the designer of Total War: Warhammer 3's well-received tutorial, at this year's Gamescom. She was accompanied by battle product owner Dave Petry, responsible for shaping the galaxy-spanning clashes players can expect in the upcoming release.
And there's a lot going on this time around, according to Dey. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is "the biggest and most complex game we've ever made", she tells me, and it's easy to see why. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 lathers the series' usual tactics with a generous spread of new systems and mechanics. On a micro scale, for instance, battles are a deluge of bullets that make use of new line-of-sight and cover systems. Tactical abilities such as aerial bombardments and powerful unit buffs can be called upon in a moment's notice, and a unit's weaponry must be matched against a complementary enemy if you hope for success.
Petr y says the need for these kinds of tools and toys became "blindingly obvious" as the team started thinking about how to get its depiction of Warhammer 40,000 right. And many of the game's biggest swings have roots in the studio's desire to accurately represent the series' horrific sci-fi setting.
Petry explains: "You quickly look at it and go, 'There are a lot of guns here, there are a lot more weapons than we're used to with Total War'. Everything has a lot more ranged firepower - though there's still a lot of melee fighting [...] We've had to re-engineer a lot of stuff to support the combat we need. The systems have been changed fundamentally so we can support the volume of fire: we simulate every bullet, bolt round, and laser beam. So we had to do a great deal well to be able to pull that off."
Dey also highlights Total War: Warhammer 40,000's new Warcore engine, saying it was needed to "make the campaign feel as big as it should be." This is, afterall, a far larger game than previous series entries, playing out across a galaxy rather than a single planet, and featuring multiple battlefields on multiple worlds that must be simulated at once.
But the team also faced challenges on a smaller scale as it sought to meet the expectations of the Warhammer 40,000 community. It's not just major factions like the series' iconic Space Marines that have loyal fans; subfactions have their own followings too. Each subfaction has its specialties - one chapter may love bikes while another leans more towards hit-and-run tactics - and the team felt it was crucial to capture each one's distinct flavour
The solution? An emphasis on unit specialisation, which Petry calls a series first. Units can be leveled up and specialised, given different weapons of your choosing such as bolt rifles or stalker rifles. Your sergeants too will feature some degree of customisation to fit your chosen fantasy.
"We're capturing something there that's so inherent to the universe and what Warhammer 40,000 is as a fan," Petry continues"To be able to engage with it in your way, to insert your fantasy into it and share it, is what it's all about. To create your own chapter or clan is super important. It's something we knew we had to do."
So, there's a lot going on. But what about that "most accessible part"? According to Dey, the studio is anticipating a lot of new players who've never touched a Total War game before, which is why it's developed what it's calling the "most approachable" tutorial it's ever made.
"There's no denying [Warhammer 40,000]] has become increasingly popular," says Petry, "That's been incredible to see ... and this game coming out within this period of popularity, there's a huge chance we'll be seeing a huge wave of new players coming to Total War.
"We want to make [Total War: Warhammer 40,000] as approachable and accessible as possible. But this is still Total war - we don't want to fundamentally change what Total War is. We want to invite people into this big tent with this grimdark setting. So, if there are going to be a lot of new players coming, let's show them why Total War is awesome."
To that end, the tutorial includes UI gating; the gradual introduction of individual systems through a dedicated campaign to slowly ease players in. Two tutorial campaigns are present in Total War: Warhammer 40,000 according to Dey, both designed to make the leap into the full campaign and other modes less daunting. These, I'm told, were planned from the start of development; an evolution of Total War: Warhammer 3's tutorial campaign, which while a much-appreciated introduction to the game's many systems was still a relatively simple venture compared to the complexity of the outstandingly large Immortal Empires campaign.
But the tutorial serves a dual purpose. As Dey notes, it also acts as an introduction to Warhammer 40,000 itself, hopefully allowing strategy fans to quickly acclimate with its setting and grimdark tone. It is, after all, a bit of a larger leap to put yourself in the shoes of galactic super soldiers than it is Three Kingdom's Cao Cao.
All this makes for what Total War: Warhammer 40,000 brand director is calling the "start of a new era" for Creative Assembly, and it's abundantly clear the team is excited by the prospect.
"It's the start of a new and frankly wild crazy adventure," Petry tells me. "We're going to take this starting release like we did with Total War: Warhammer back in the day. We're going to start relatively small and we're … going to fill it up, until someone drags us away, with more and more of this stuff. With enthusiasm and a new arsenal of tools ... It's version 1.0, there are going to be some bumps, but we're going to sincerely do our best to make something fantastic."

item.title: If you're familiar with the lineage of Rebel Wolves, the studio behind the recently-released The Blood of Dawnwalker, it may not surprise you to learn that a lot of the game's players are also fans of a certain other medieval fantasy RPG. Read more
item.description:
If you're familiar with the lineage of Rebel Wolves, the studio behind the recently-released The Blood of Dawnwalker, it may not surprise you to learn that a lot of the game's players are also fans of a certain other medieval fantasy RPG.
According to new data by industry analysts at Alinea Analytics, nearly 58 percent of Dawnwalker players have also played The Witcher 3. Rebel Wolves, of course, is a team made up of many former Witcher developers and CD Projekt Red alumni. The games share a few other similarities, too, such as being centred around a protagonist with superpowers they didn't ask for in a world that doesn't always like or appreciate them.
Analyst Rhys Elliott also revealed in the same report that Poland is the game's second-largest market on Steam, with 11 percent of players. The US is far ahead at number one, though, with 34 percent. It's clear local players showed up, given that both Rebel Wolves and CDPR are Polish studios.
Speaking of shared audiences, The Blood of Dawnwalker's players cross-over with a number of other recent releases in the same or similar genres. According to the report, 13 percent of players have played Mortal Shell 2, and 9 percent have played Onimusha: Way of the Sword.
Rebel Wolves recently announced Dawnwalker has sold over one million copies in its first three days on sale. Alinea estimates 410,000 of those sales were made on Steam, noting it "also did well" on GOG, the DRM-free PC game store. Given how large the game's PC audience appears to be, Dawnwalker has a growing mod scene, though the most popular mod so far removes its main time mechanic.
In the Eurogamer review of The Blood of Dawnwalker, Bertie was happy with how the game used said time mechanic to create meaningful stakes, even if that brilliance doesn't always come across elsewhere in the game.

item.description:
With the gameplay reveal of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake happening earlier today, thousands of people from around of the world have taken their first look at the latest entry in the beloved Nintendo series. The most immediate reaction from the masses? A combination of confusion and delight at the new look.
The game has been created with a modern new aesthetic, one that appears to be striking the balance between the iconic original and modern tools at Nintendo's disposal. The result is a game that looks familiar but different, with highly details landscapes and faces. Link, especially, has an interesting look to him.
It's worth noting up front that there's a lot of positively surrounding the reveal. Multiple fans of the original have taken to social media to express their delight.
That Ocarina Of Time Remake looks like perfection. Legit goosebumps
Wow. Zelda looks absolutely phenomenal
Nintendo's remakes look like what the original artists wanted to make, but couldn't because of the limitations of the era. Personally, I like it. It feels like playing with the promo art from strategy guides and magazine spreads. But it also means these new remakes look anachronistic in 2026.
The textures in this game are really giving kind of like a lovely hand-made model look without being something like claymation. It’s almost like glazed ceramics figurines.[image or embed]
However, these positive sentiments are matched by many detractors, some of whom making a connection between this new reveal and the Unreal Engine Nintendo joke mock-ups from the past.
ocarina of time remake looks like one of those “what if we remade zelda in unreal engine” 😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭
The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time remake pic.twitter.com/R4QrmY5iuG

The Legend of Zelda: Oceania of Time (2026) pic.twitter.com/WOxDZ8p2CP
Many of the criticisms of the visuals are levied at Link himself. Other characters, like Zelda or NPCs found out in the world, are actually leaning more positive!
PRINCESS ZELDA IS SO PRETTY OH MY GOD pic.twitter.com/gpEnbDMsad

item.title: It's been argued that Battlefield 6's Redsec battle royale off-shoot is a response to Call of Duty's popular Warzone mode, and today's news is another indication of that. Read more
item.description:
It's been argued that Battlefield 6's Redsec battle royale off-shoot is a response to Call of Duty's popular Warzone mode, and today's news is another indication of that.
Battlefield Studios has unveiled Rapid Royale, Redsec's version of Warzone's Resurgence. If you're unfamiliar, Resurgence takes place on dedicated maps that are far smaller than the main mode's large playground, and offers many ways to respawn after death. The pace is significantly faster with more frequent firefights as a result, and these are the principles guiding the Redsec version, too.
Rapid Royale features a reduced player count and is likewise only available on maps smaller than the main mode's. The circles move faster, too, further pushing players closer and closer together. Expect matches that finish quickly, notably a lot shorter than the main mode.
Rapid Royale is one of several new additions coming to Battlefield 6 and Redsec with Season 5, which does not yet have a release date. While we wait for that, Season 4's final stage - named Tidal Strike - kicks off 15th September and introduces the first iteration of proximity chat.
As the name suggests, the feature allows players to communicate with others around them who are not part of their squad. It's initially available only in battle royale, with the plan to expand it to Battlefield 6 multiplayer down the road.
Season 4 has been a major step forward for Battlefield 6. It brought naval combat to Battlefield 6 alongside the game's biggest map yet. The season's second stage was even more exciting, introducing a Top Gun collaboration, a remake of Wake Island, two-seater jets and a reimagined Carrier Assault mode dubbed Carrier Strike. Season 5 has a vague 'winter 2026' target, and is expected to bring three new maps to the game alongside other unannounced additions.

item.title: Gameplay has been released for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake at long last during today's Zelda 40th anniversary Nintendo Direct. It'll be releasing on the Nintendo Switch 2 on the 5th November. Read more
item.description:
Gameplay has been released for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake at long last during today's Zelda 40th anniversary Nintendo Direct. It'll be releasing on the Nintendo Switch 2 on the 5th November.
The gameplay, narrated by producer Eiji Aonuma, shows what looks to be a largely faithful recreation of the original 3rd person adventure classic, albeit with some modern advancements. For one, Link can jump manually now, and the whole game has been brought to life in a new engine.
A lot of classic sounds and animations also appear to have been either brought over untouched, or recreated faithfully. The famous chest opening animation, for example, looks very much the same as it did all those years ago. Just with that newer aesthetic applied to it.
A particularly cool feature was also shown in regards to playing Link's iconic ocarina. Players can turn on their microphone and hum, whistle, or sing the various tunes required for gameplay changes to occur.
That's where the gameplay presentation largely ends. Some final notes on there being a lot of work on audio capped off the gameplay. Cutscences will be fully-voiced, and the theme of this new Zelda remake will be added to the Nintendo Music platform.
There will also be a Zelda notes companion app available for this game, allowing you to take screenshots and venture on mini-quests of discovery for points. There is also an ocarina music feature allowing you to make your own tracks, and a quiz.
Finally, there will also be two new amiibos for the Ocarina of Time remake, both of which will unlock in-game masks. Lovely.

item.description:
Can you believe it? Link (the green one) is 40 this year, yet his boundless enthusiasm for adventure still hasn't waned. My boundless enthusiasm, meanwhile, waned decades back, so it's clearly something in the Hyrule air. ANYWAY, to celebrate the Zelda series' 40th anniversary, Nintendo has released a special Direct showcase (the first of two planned for this week), featuring a "variety of The Legend of Zelda-related information".
That, we now know, included a full reveal for its Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake following its somewhat controversial unveiling earlier this year, a new Zelda-themed Switch 2, a couple of amiibo, a musical tour, and more. For the full rundown of announcements, cast your eyes below...
A classic reborn, and all of that. Not everyone loved the semi-realistic look Nintendo appeared to be going for when it unveiled Switch 2's Ocarina of Time remake earlier this year. But we've now had a chance to see it properly in action, and it's certainly different, opting for a moody, misty, fairytale vibe unlike any Zelda we've seen before.
New features include a manual jump and the ability to hum ocarina tunes into the Switch 2's mic rather than tapping them out. Or you could toot a tune on an actual ocarina if you have one lying around. It's fully voiced too (which is going to take some getting used to), and supports Zelda Notes on the Switch app. As for when it's out, it's coming 5th November this year.
Of course, it wouldn't be a new Nintendo release without new amiibo to go with it, and that's exactly what we've got. New amiibo based on the Ocarina of Time remake's interpretation of Young Link and Young Zelda are due to release at some currently undisclosed point later this year.
Your Switch 2 not Zelda-y enough for your liking? Well, you'll have the opportunity to change that on 29th October. Nintendo has announced a new Zelda-themed console, with Link-ish green Joy-Cons and a triangular pattern inspired by the golden glow of the Triforce. Plus, there's a similarly styled Switch 2 Pro Controller and carry case coming too.
If you're a fan of the Zelda series' music (and frankly, who isn't?), then you'll be able to hear some of its most beloved tunes played live in concert starting early next year. Nintendo's preparing a worldwide orchestral tour that begins in Tokyo, Japan, on 23rd January before heading to North America, Europe, and Australia, with a UK date set for 3rd April in London.
We've all been wondering how Nintendo might be looking to tackle its (I think) first live-action video game adaptation since 1993's Super Mario Bros. movie, and, well, we still don't know. Today brought the news the Zelda movie - which stars Benjamin Evan Ainsworth as Link, Bo Bragason as Princess Zelda, and Sam Neill in one of his last appearances - won't have a subtitle. Why? Zelda creator Shigeru Miyamoto says we'll find out when it releases in cinemas on 30th April next year. Thanks Miyamoto!
If you're a collectibles fan, it looks like there's plenty to keep you busy as Zelda's 40th anniversary continues. Nintendo flashed up a range of Zelda-themed bits at the start of the show, but its post-Direct press release has gone into more detail. There's a 1,750-piece Link & Epona Lego set arriving in spring 2027. Also on the way is an electronic Master Sword courtesy of Hasbro (it's 27 inches long and features 15 touch- and motion-activated sounds, apparently), but if you prefer your noises to be more musical, you've some additional choices. Nintendo is releasing a playable Ocarina in the "future", and there's an electric version from Hori too, if you're less musically inclined.
